title: Structural exponential transient bound with later finite-horizon polynomial compiler
statement: CURRENT STATUS: The structural exponential-in-T estimate remains valid for every elementary network with bounded coefficients. NEW P3 66BC05 pays exponentially small exits against that growth for its compiled rates/horizon and obtains polynomial robust FINITE-HORIZON costs. This is a sharper design-specific operation,not a claim that the general exponential estimate was polynomial or that arbitrary-time perturbed stationary costs are closed. HISTORICAL VALID ROUTE: For ANY finite mass-action network with at mostTWO molecules on EACH side and actual channel constants<=3/2,positive total-population increments have zero/unimolecular propensities; quadratic propensities cannot increaseN. Discarding negative changes gives Q(1+N)^j<=C_j(1+N)^j,C_j=6j3^j J. Stopped finite-state Dynkin/Gronwall andj1 yield vanishing O(n^-1) population-exit probability on finite horizons. On bounded-population sets total labelled intensity is bounded,so internal/null firings cannot accumulate. Hence ALL admitted independent coefficient choices are nonexplosive,without weak reversibility or an invariant law. Moreover E(1+N_T)^j<=(1+N0)^j exp(C_jT),and expected ALL firings<=3J(1+N0)^2/2 timesint_0^T exp(C2t)dt. These finite bounds are EXPONENTIAL in physicalT; they do not pay polynomialW full-cycle costs whenT is polynomialW,and do not imply perturbed positive recurrence or stationary accuracy.
